engagement.judgement: Opening entry; Scl-AbII is a research antibody, not a tile member, so product_in_model is false.

engagement.magnitude_basis: bone formation (rat histomorphometry) vs serum P1NP rise
engagement.population: Healthy men and postmenopausal women (single-dose phase 1)

engagement.short: Bone formation markers rose in humans
engagement.quote: Dose-related increases in the bone-formation markers procollagen type 1 N-propeptide (P1NP), bone-specific alkaline phosphatase (BAP), and osteocalcin were observed, along with a dose-related decrease in the bone-resorption marker serum C-telopeptide (sCTx), resulting in a large anabolic window.
engagement.reason: Bone formation rose as rats predicted
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: model side is Li 2009 (bone formation by histomorphometry), human side serum formation markers, read as downstream of Wnt activation. Healthy volunteers count for engagement.

efficacy.population: Unselected (postmenopausal women with low BMD or osteoporosis)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Registry NCT00896532 results posted 2018-12-14. Earliest public: Amgen/UCB press release 2011-04-21 (https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/amgen-and-ucb-announce-positive-phase-2-results-of-amg-785cdp7851-in-patients-with-postmenopausal-osteoporosis-pmo-120335159.html) stating the primary endpoint (12-month lumbar spine BMD) was met; McClung 2014 sets the status.

efficacy.judgement: Paired by me with Li 2009; the rat surrogate is bone mass, matched to the phase 2 primary endpoint (lumbar spine BMD). FRAME (2016, fracture outcome) was positive, so outcome_tested is positive; blosozumab phase 2 (2015) also raised BMD. Quote is the first part of a longer abstract sentence.

patient_trials.quote: Blosozumab treatment resulted in statistically significant dose-related increases in spine, femoral neck, and total hip BMD as compared with placebo.

At 12 months, new vertebral fractures had occurred in 16 of 3321 patients (0.5%) in the romosozumab group, as compared with 59 of 3322 (1.8%) in the placebo group (representing a 73% lower risk with romosozumab; P<0.001).

Over a period of 24 months, a 48% lower risk of new vertebral fractures was observed in the romosozumab-to-alendronate group (6.2% [127 of 2046 patients]) than in the alendronate-to-alendronate group (11.9% [243 of 2047 patients]) (P<0.001).

Most endpoints were null and plaque volume fell, but FDA reads the necrotic-plaque increase as consistent with the human signal, so retro with source_calls_it partial rather than contra. Standard rat and monkey tox silence on MI/stroke is not scored: healthy animals cannot show ischemic events.
